title: Word Types & Grammar Fundamentals
description: Identify nouns, verbs, adjectives and grammatical fundamentals in A1 German.

questions.question: Welches Wort ist ein Nomen?
questions.english: Which word is a noun?
questions.explanation: 'Haus' (house) is a noun and is always capitalized in German. 'laufen' is a verb, while 'schnell' and 'schön' are adjectives/adverbs.

questions.question: Welches Wort ist ein Verb (Tätowort)?
questions.english: Which word is a verb (action word)?
questions.explanation: 'sprechen' (to speak) is an action verb in infinitive form (-en ending).

questions.question: Welches Wort wird im Deutschen IMMER großgeschrieben?
questions.english: Which word is ALWAYS capitalized in German?
questions.explanation: All nouns in German must begin with a capital letter. 'Schule' (school) is a noun!

questions.question: Was ist das richtige Gegenteil von 'klein'?
questions.english: What is the correct opposite of 'small'?

questions.question: Welches Wort ist ein Adjektiv?
questions.english: Which word is an adjective?
questions.explanation: 'glücklich' (happy) is an adjective describing feelings or states.

title: Articles & Noun Gender (Der, Die, Das)
description: Select the correct German definite or indefinite article for everyday A1 grammar nouns.

questions.question: ___ Haus ist sehr schön und groß.
questions.english: The house is very beautiful and big.
questions.explanation: 'Haus' is neuter in German (das Haus) in the Nominative case.

questions.question: Wo ist ___ Bahnhof, bitte?
questions.english: Where is the train station, please?

questions.question: Ich kaufe ___ neuen Computer für meine Arbeit.
questions.english: I am buying a new computer for my work.
questions.explanation: 'Computer' is masculine, and as a direct object (Accusative), 'ein' becomes 'einen'.

questions.question: Hier steht ___ Tasse Kaffee für dich.
questions.english: Here is a cup of coffee for you.
questions.explanation: 'Tasse' is feminine (die Tasse), so the indefinite article in Nominative is 'eine'.

questions.question: Wir sehen ___ Kinder im Park spielen.
questions.english: We see the children playing in the park.
questions.explanation: In plural, the definite article is always 'die' for Nominative and Accusative cases.

title: Present Tense Verbs & Personal Pronouns
description: Choose the correct conjugated present tense verb form (Präsens) or personal pronoun.

questions.question: Ich ___ aus Deutschland und lerne Spanisch.
questions.english: I come from Germany and learn Spanish.
questions.explanation: For 1st person singular ('ich'), regular verbs end in '-e' (komme).

questions.question: Woher ___ du ursprünglich?
questions.english: Where do you originally come from?
questions.explanation: For 2nd person singular informal ('du'), regular verbs end in '-st' (kommst).

questions.question: Meine Schwester ___ als Lehrerin in Berlin.
questions.english: My sister works as a teacher in Berlin.
questions.explanation: For 3rd person singular ('sie'), stems ending in -t add an '-et' for easy pronunciation (arbeitet).

questions.question: Wir ___ heute Abend eine Pizza im Restaurant.
questions.english: We are eating a pizza in the restaurant tonight.
questions.explanation: For 1st person plural ('wir'), verbs keep their infinitive form (essen).

questions.question: Was ___ ihr am Wochenende machen?
questions.english: What do you all want to do on the weekend?
questions.explanation: The modal verb 'wollen' in 2nd person plural ('ihr') is conjugated as 'wollt'.

title: Sentence Missing Word Fill-Up: Essential Core Verbs
description: Fill in the missing word! Type the exact missing grammar word or conjugated verb directly into the box.

questions.sentenceAfter: aus Frankfurt und ich wohne jetzt in Berlin.
questions.english: I come from Frankfurt and I live in Berlin now.
questions.explanation: For 'ich', remove '-en' from 'kommen' and add '-e': ich komme.

questions.english: My family and I live in a big, cozy apartment.
questions.explanation: The subject 'Meine Familie und ich' equals 'wir' (we), taking the infinitive form 'wohnen'.

questions.sentenceAfter: heute sehr glücklich, weil die Sonne scheint.
questions.hint: Infinitive: sein (3rd person singular / she is)
questions.english: Anna is very happy today because the sun is shining.
questions.explanation: 'Sein' is irregular: for er/sie/es, the present tense form is 'ist'.

questions.sentenceAfter: du am liebsten zum Frühstück? Kaffee oder Tee?
questions.english: What do you prefer to drink for breakfast? Coffee or tea?
questions.explanation: For 'du', regular verbs attach the ending '-st': trinkst.

questions.sentenceAfter: jeden Tag mit großer Begeisterung Deutsch!
questions.english: We learn German every day with great enthusiasm!
questions.explanation: For 'wir', verbs keep their full infinitive ending '-en': lernen.

title: Sentence Missing Word Fill-Up: Question Words & Prepositions
description: Test your grasp of German question words (Wer, Wo, Wie, Wann, Woher) and core prepositions in natural sentences.

questions.sentenceAfter: liegt eigentlich Berlin? Ist es im Osten Deutschlands?
questions.hint: Question word asking for a location: 'Where?'
questions.english: Where is Berlin actually located? Is it in the east of Germany?
questions.explanation: 'Wo' asks for a static location (where is something located).

questions.hint: Question word: 'How' (as in What is your name / How are you called?)
questions.english: What is your last name? (literally: How are you called with family name?)
questions.explanation: In German, one asks 'Wie heißen Sie?' using 'Wie' (how) instead of 'what'.

questions.sentenceAfter: kommen Ihre glücklichen Freunde? Aus Österreich?
questions.hint: Question word asking for origin: 'From where?'
questions.english: Where do your happy friends come from? From Austria?
questions.explanation: 'Woher' specifically inquiries about geographical or cultural origin (from where).

questions.sentenceBefore: Wir fahren Morgen mit dem schnellen Zug
questions.hint: Preposition used when traveling to cities and countries without articles: 'to'
questions.english: Tomorrow we are traveling with the fast train to Hamburg and Bremen.
questions.explanation: When traveling toward a city or neuter country, German uses the preposition 'nach'.

questions.english: When does the interactive German course start today?
questions.explanation: 'Wann' is the question word used to ask about days, times, and schedule moments.
